abort.invalid_unique_id: Could not read the device's serial number
abort.not_wireless_debugging: This is not a wireless debugging service
abort.reauth_successful: Paired again. The connection is back.
abort.wrong_device: The device at this address is a different device than the one being re-paired.

error.cannot_connect: Could not open a wireless debugging session. If this Home Assistant has never been paired with the device, enter the pairing port and code.
error.not_advertised: The device isn't advertising wireless debugging. Turn on Developer options > Wireless debugging on the device and try again.
error.pairing_failed: Pairing was rejected. Check the code, and keep the pairing dialog open on the device while you submit.
error.pairing_port_required: Enter the pairing port shown next to the code
error.pairing_unreachable: Could not reach the pairing port. Is the pairing dialog still open on the device?
error.helper_install_failed: Installing the helper app failed (see the log). Untick the box to finish setup without it; you can install it later from its update entity.
error.pairing_code_required: Enter the pairing code shown on the device

data_description.pairing_code: The six-digit Wi-Fi pairing code. Leave empty if this Home Assistant is already paired with the device.
data_description.pairing_port: The port after the colon in the IP address and port shown with the code (not the port on the main Wireless debugging screen).

pair.description: On the device at {host}, open Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with pairing code, then enter the port and code it shows. The pairing is remembered, so this is only needed once.
pair.title: Pair with the device

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the Android TV. Wireless debugging must be turned on under Developer options.

helper.title: Install the helper app
helper.description: Android turns wireless debugging off whenever the device restarts. The Wireless ADB Helper app (version {version}) turns it back on at boot and every 15 minutes, so Home Assistant can always reach the device. Home Assistant installs it over the connection it just opened, grants it permission to change that setting, and keeps it updated.

data_description.install_helper: Recommended. Without it, wireless debugging stays off after every restart until someone turns it on by hand.

reauth_confirm.title: Pair {name} again
reauth_confirm.description: {name} no longer accepts Home Assistant's key (this happens on some firmwares after a restart). On the device at {host}, open Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with pairing code, then enter the port and code it shows.

data_description.pairing_port: The port after the colon in the IP address and port shown with the code.

data_description.relaunch_helper: If the TV is on but wireless debugging is off for 3 minutes, launch the helper through the Android TV Remote integration (which doesn't need ADB). Retried every 5 minutes.
data_description.relaunch_entity: Leave empty to use the Android TV Remote entity set up for the same address.
